title: The projection formula
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism of schemes. For $E\in D_{\text{QCoh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$ and $K\in D_{\text{QCoh}}(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ the canonical map $Rf_*(E)\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Y}^{\mathbb L}K\to Rf_*(E\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^{\mathbb L}Lf^*K)$ is an isomorphism; in particular, for an invertible $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module $\mathcal{N}$, $Rf_*(E)\otimes\mathcal{N}\cong Rf_*(E\otimes f^*\mathcal{N})$.

proof.text: The canonical projection map is natural in E and K, and the isomorphism assertion can be checked after restriction to an open covering of Y. By [lem-pc-projection-locality], it is enough to prove the assertion when Y is affine, Y=Spec(A).

source.place: Equation 20.54.2.1 (cohomology-equation-projection-formula-map), and the locality reduction in perfect.tex Lemma 36.22.1 (Tag 08EU)

proof.text: Assume Y=\operatorname{Spec}(A). By [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence], M\mapsto\widetilde M is an equivalence of triangulated categories D(A)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y) sending A[k] to \mathcal O_Y[k]; being an equivalence it preserves direct sums, which exist in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y) by [lem-pc-derived-qcoh-direct-sums]. Let T(M) be the property that the canonical map is an isomorphism for K=\widetilde M (E fixed). (i) T is closed under direct sums: Lf^* and E\otimes^{\mathbb L}- are left adjoints, hence preserve direct sums; by [lem-pc-derived-pullback-tensor-qcoh] each E\otimes^{\mathbb L}Lf^*\widetilde{M_i} lies in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X), so Rf_* preserves their direct sum by [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-direct-sums]; by naturality in K the map for \bigoplus M_i is the direct sum of the maps for the M_i. (ii) If two of the vertices of a distinguished triangle in D(A) satisfy T, so does the third: all functors involved are exact, the canonical maps form a morphism of distinguished triangles, and the five lemma applies. (iii) T is closed under retracts. (iv) T(A[k]) holds: for K=\mathcal O_Y[k] both sides are canonically Rf_*(E)[k] and the canonical map is the identity under these identifications. By [lem-pc-derived-module-free-generation], T(M) holds for every M in D(A), hence the map is an isomorphism for every K in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y).

source.place: Lemma 36.22.1 (Tag 08EU), second and third paragraphs; Lemma 36.3.5 (Tag 06Z0); Lemma 36.4.5 (Tag 08DZ); More on Algebra, Remark 15.60.11 (Tag 09PB)

proof.text: For an invertible O_Y-module N, regard N as N[0] in D_QCoh(O_Y). Specializing the derived formula to K=N[0] gives the displayed ordinary tensor formula because N is locally free, so tensoring with N is already derived and Lf^*N=f^*N.
